sentences.text: The occurrence of the offence is shown on 13 July 2025.

The offences alleged are under Sections 26(2)(iv), 27(3)(d), 27(3)(e),
30(2)(a), 3(1)(zz)(iv) and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006 (for short 'the said Act') and under Section 123, 223, 274 and 275 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
The informant is one Rajesh Namdeo Bade, aged 50 years.
5. With the assistance of the learned Advocates for the parties, I have perused the FIR and the record available with the Court.
6. It appears that the name of the Applicant is disclosed in the FIR.
It further appears that the Applicant is the supplier of the said contraband which is banned substance under the provisions of the said Act.
The said contraband was duly seized and no further recoveries are to be effected.
Mr Lavte, learned APP would not dispute such position.

7. Ms Sonawane, learned Advocate for the Applicant would draw attention of the Court to the order dated 23 July 2025 in Anticipatory Bail Application No.1248/2025, thereby similarly placed Applicant was protected by the order of interim protection.

Such  1409.25aba  (3)
protection was on the basis of the order passed by this Court on 22 July 2025 in Anticipatory Bail Application No.857/2025 and connected proceedings concerning contraband i.e. Gutkha.
The Applicant has one criminal antecedent.
In this regard, learned Advocate for the Applicant has placed before the Court an order dated 18 July 2025, passed by the Sessions Court, Ahmednagar.

Considering the factual matrix as noted above, prima facie, in my view, the Applicant deserves some protection at this stage.
In view of the above, I pass the following order:
 ORDER (i) Until adjourned date of hearing, in the event of arrest of the Applicant Atik Alias Akib Alias Don Mohammed Shaikh in connection with C.R. No.0354/2025 registered with Akole Police Station,
District Ahilyanagar, for the offences punishable under Sections 26(2)(iv), 27(3)(d), 27(3)(e),
30(2)(a), 3(1)(zz)(iv) and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'the said Act')
and under Section 123, 223, 274 and 275 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, he is directed to be released on bail on furnishing PR bond in 1409.25aba the sum of Rs. 20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) each with one or more sureties in the like amount.
(ii) The Applicant shall attend the concerned Police Station on every Monday at 11.30 am, until the further orders and shall cooperate with the investigation.
(iii) The Applicant shall furnish details of residential address and other contact details such as the mobile number etc. to the concerned Police Station.
If there is any change in the contact details, the same shall be immediately informed to the concerned Police Station.
(iv) The Applicant shall not leave the jurisdiction of the competent Court without prior permission,
until further orders.
(v) He shall not contact and/or influence the witness/es and/or tamper with the evidence in any manner whatsoever.
9.
List this Application for further consideration/hearing alongwith Anticipatory Bail Application No.857/2025 and connected Anticipatory Bail Applications on 08 September 2025.
10. The protection granted today in favour of the Applicant shall continue till the adjourned date of hearing.
